name: Croma GOV-TECH AI Hackathon
theme: Government technology on official public data

judging.notes: One prize only; the other eleven are listed alphabetically, unranked.

required_tech: Croma Platform via API or MCP

entries.name: Análisis de negocios con gobierno, línea automotriz
entries.tagline: Public-procurement intelligence for the automotive sector: what the state buys and from whom.

entries.name: AUTODATA
entries.tagline: Telegram bot that checks a used car and its seller against six Peruvian sources and returns a verdict, fair price and negotiation script.

entries.name: Contraparte
entries.tagline: Due diligence on companies and people across Colombia, Mexico and Peru, each datum tied to its official source.

entries.name: Creva Score
entries.tagline: Explainable credit score for women entrepreneurs without credit history, built from official records.

entries.name: GraphAudit
entries.tagline: Corporate-control map: which individuals concentrate control over a contracting entity's suppliers, prioritized for review.

entries.name: Mallanet Verify
entries.tagline: MCP server that screens an NGO's volunteers against public sources and stores a Pass/Alert/Fail report.

entries.name: RASTRO
entries.tagline: Risk file on any contractor or entity, crossing six sources in parallel with source and lookup date per finding.

entries.name: TRAZA
entries.tagline: Research agent turning a plain-language procurement question into an auditable case file.

entries.name: Trazo
entries.tagline: Interactive live graph of public procurement: entities, suppliers, contracts and sanctions.

organizer_takeaways.claim: Seven of twelve projects targeted public procurement; none stopped at contract search — all crossed corporate registry, financials and disciplinary records against the process.

Almost every team wrote its own counter-explanation (prioritize not accuse; cite source and date; do not penalize missing voluntary data). Once data is easy to cross, the judgment used to read it becomes the product.
The winner was chosen because one analysis reads two ways: opportunity for a small business, red flag for a citizen — one engine, two products.

curator_notes: Strong base-rate data: complete roster with one winner. Procurement was the crowded lane (7/12) and still produced the winner — differentiation came from dual use and autonomous action, not lane choice.
